findings.title: Attribution-header change lacks required security sign-off
findings.problem: security-practices.md and the git-workflow review checklist mark any add/rewrite of X-CodeMie-Project and related attribution headers, or a new derivation source for them, as CRITICAL requiring explicit security-reviewer sign-off. This change adds a Cowork project pin and a CodeMie-funded declaration (Project, Project-Source, subscription_type codemie) via coworkFundingHeaders / requestHeaders / cowork-attribution.ts; record.md states sign-off is not obtained.
findings.impact: Project and billing attribution changes could merge without the documented review gate.
findings.recommendation: Obtain and record the security reviewers' sign-off on the PR, marked CRITICAL in the description, before merge; record the outcome via fix_evidence decision.

findings.title: EPMCDME-17410 AC1 only partially met for legacy sessions
findings.problem: Funding headers are sent only when a served mark exists and the pin source is linked_folder or profile (cowork-attribution.ts coworkFundingSource). Sessions with no mark (collected before marks existed or mark pruned mid-session), pin source none (spool-bound before the pin, or bound differing from resolved project) and non-ASCII projects fall back to the legacy Project header and are stored unknown. A pruned mark also makes later requests of the same session drop funding.
findings.impact: The ticket requires every sent Cowork session to be codemie; these sessions remain unknown and are not counted as CodeMie spend.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the gap is accepted (and amend AC1/record) or add a mechanism for these sessions, e.g. keep funding once a funded request was sent, and cover the cases explicitly.

findings.title: Hard-link failure other than EEXIST blocks session processing
findings.problem: saveCoworkAttribution rethrows any link() error that is not EEXIST (EPERM/ENOTSUP/EXDEV/ENOSYS on filesystems without hard links). The error propagates out of pinAttribution, which runs before any event is appended. Reachability of such a filesystem for the analytics state dir was not confirmed.
findings.impact: On such a filesystem the pin is never written, pinAttribution throws every tick and the session's analytics are never appended.
findings.recommendation: On EPERM/ENOTSUP/EXDEV/ENOSYS fall back to a non-overwriting publish (e.g. writeFile with flag 'wx' then reload), then return the pin in effect; rethrow only unknown errors.

findings.title: Unreadable-pin recovery can overwrite a valid pin
findings.problem: On EEXIST with an unreadable file, saveCoworkAttribution does rename(temp, path), overwriting unconditionally. Two racers that both see the corrupt file both rename, and a valid pin written between the load and the rename is overwritten, so the write-once guarantee does not hold and the racers return different pins. Reachability unconfirmed (needs a corrupt pin file).
findings.impact: Events can be stamped with a project the pin file no longer holds, moving a session between projects.
findings.recommendation: Remove the corrupt file then retry link (looping once), or reload after the rename and return the loaded pin so every racer agrees.
